title: ACES reproducible related-work comparison protocol
purpose: Compare the observed, revision-pinned capabilities of ACES and selected precedent systems without converting unlike scopes into a universal quality ranking.
inclusion_criteria: Include ACES as the assessed system and independently identify each precedent named by issue 728.
Include a precedent only when an originating publication, maintaining-body standard, official documentation, or source repository supports cell-level extraction.
Use a fixed system version or full Git revision and retain the exact locator for every observation.
Retain systems with different purposes in separate scope strata; cross-stratum observations are descriptive only.
exclusion_criteria: Exclude systems represented only by secondary summaries or unpinned mutable material.
Exclude composite identities such as Cyber DEM/FOM or CRACK/VSDL; related systems receive independent rows.
Exclude feature counts that cannot be mapped to an axis rubric and primary-source rationale.
Exclude repository popularity, marketing language, and roadmap intent as implementation or adoption evidence.

scope_strata.label: Scenario authoring and realization
scope_strata.description: Languages whose primary unit is an authored cyber-range scenario or infrastructure intent.

scope_strata.label: Agent simulation environment
scope_strata.description: An executable environment centered on agent actions, observations, rewards, and episodes.

scope_strata.label: Security playbook orchestration
scope_strata.description: A standardized workflow-exchange language rather than a cyber-range scenario language.

scope_strata.label: Federation data exchange
scope_strata.description: Runtime cyber object/event exchange and its HLA-specific federation realization.

systems.name: ACES
systems.inclusion_rationale: The subject system, pinned to the pre-implementation dev revision and assessed against repository authority plus executable delivery evidence.

systems.name: OCR SDL
systems.inclusion_rationale: A deployed YAML cyber-range authoring language with official documentation and a revision-pinned parser implementation.

systems.name: CybORG
systems.inclusion_rationale: An executable autonomous-cyber-operations gym explicitly named by the issue and grounded in an originating paper plus source.

systems.name: CACAO 2.0
systems.inclusion_rationale: A standardized security-playbook language that supplies a workflow and governance comparison boundary.

systems.name: Cyber DEM
systems.inclusion_rationale: The solution-independent cyber object/event model named by the issue, assessed separately from its HLA realization.

systems.name: Cyber FOM
systems.inclusion_rationale: The HLA-specific implementation of the Cyber DEM, independently attributable and standardized after the base model.

systems.name: CRACK
systems.inclusion_rationale: A TOSCA/Datalog cyber-range scenario framework with formal verification and deployment testing evidence.

systems.name: VSDL
systems.inclusion_rationale: A constraint-based virtual scenario language with SMT semantics, temporal guards, composition, and generated deployment scripts.

axes.label: Expressive breadth
axes.construct: Distinct authored concerns representable within the system's declared scope, demonstrated by constructs and representative tasks rather than field counts.

rubric.0: No authored representation for the representative concerns.
rubric.1: One narrow concern family or indirect representation.
rubric.2: Several concern families with material documented omissions.
rubric.3: Broad, typed coverage across the representative concerns with explicit limits.

axes.label: Semantic precision
axes.construct: Defined meaning, reference rules, ambiguity control, and semantic invariants, independent of parser strictness.

rubric.0: Meaning is informal or unavailable for the assessed constructs.
rubric.1: Basic structural meaning with substantial ambiguity or implicit references.
rubric.2: Documented semantic rules and validations for major constructs.
rubric.3: Explicit formal or normative semantics with cross-reference and invariant treatment.

axes.label: Formal analyzability
axes.construct: Explicit formal models and executable analyses over authored artifacts, not ordinary schema validation.

rubric.0: No formal model or executable formal analysis was observed.
rubric.1: Formal fragments or lightweight invariants without whole-scenario analysis.
rubric.2: Substantial formalization or analysis over a bounded subset.
rubric.3: Executable solver/model analysis is central to validation or generation.

axes.label: Concrete-syntax soundness
axes.construct: Defined source profile, safe parsing, closed shape, reference checks, diagnostics, and negative-case rejection.

rubric.0: No concrete authoring syntax or validation boundary applies.
rubric.1: Syntax is described but negative behavior or closure is weakly evidenced.
rubric.2: Implemented parser/schema checks cover common positive and negative cases.
rubric.3: Bounded parser, closed structural and semantic validation, diagnostics, and negative controls are evidenced.

axes.label: Composition and versioning
axes.construct: Reuse, imports, identity, evolution, compatibility, migration, and version-bound composition.

rubric.0: No reusable or versioned composition surface was observed.
rubric.1: Ad hoc reuse or release versioning without composition semantics.
rubric.2: Reusable units or version identity with bounded compatibility rules.
rubric.3: Explicit composition plus version, compatibility, and evolution semantics.

axes.label: Experiment design
axes.construct: Tasks, factors, allocation, randomization, measures, studies, and validity limits as declared research constructs.

rubric.0: No experiment-design construct was observed within the declared scope.
rubric.1: Objectives or evaluation hooks without a controlled design model.
rubric.2: Several explicit design constructs with documented external or missing obligations.
rubric.3: Versioned task/study/run design with allocation, measures, provenance, and validity boundaries.

axes.label: Participant modeling
axes.construct: Actions, observations, visibility, episodes, outcomes, and multi-participant interaction beyond generic roles.

rubric.1: Roles, actors, or static knowledge without action/observation lifecycle.
rubric.2: Explicit action, observation, visibility, or episode constructs with material gaps.
rubric.3: Executed action/observation/reward/episode behavior with partial-observability evidence.

axes.label: Provenance and evidence
axes.construct: Evidence identity, lineage, integrity, redaction, disclosure, and derivation rather than the mere existence of logs.

rubric.0: No structured provenance or evidence surface was observed.
rubric.1: Logs, timestamps, or metadata without full evidence lineage.
rubric.2: Structured provenance/evidence for major outputs with bounded gaps.
rubric.3: Versioned evidence identity, lineage, integrity/disclosure, and derivation surfaces.

axes.label: Interoperability
axes.construct: Defined exchange or conformance boundaries between independent implementations, not format export or backend count alone.

rubric.0: No independent exchange or conformance boundary was observed.
rubric.1: A single implementation or informal adapter boundary.
rubric.2: Published interface/profile or multiple implementations without full independent conformance evidence.
rubric.3: Standardized exchange/conformance boundary with independent implementation or federation evidence.

axes.label: Usability
axes.construct: Predeclared authoring-task completion, effort, errors, diagnostics, documentation support, and author-population limits.

rubric.0: No authoring surface or task evidence applies.
rubric.1: Examples or maintainer walkthroughs only; no independent author evidence.
rubric.2: Documented workflows and task support with limited user evidence.
rubric.3: Independent, disclosed author-task study with completion, effort, and error measures.

axes.label: Implementation maturity
axes.construct: Shipped executable behavior, releases, conformance evidence, maintenance, and independent use rather than accepted designs.

rubric.0: Concept or prose only for the assessed surface.
rubric.2: Maintained implementation with releases or operational use but limited independent conformance/adoption evidence.
rubric.3: Mature maintained implementation with release, operational, and independent-use or conformance evidence.

axes.label: Governance and community
axes.construct: Standards/governance process, independent participation, adoption, and maintenance continuity rather than repository popularity.

rubric.0: No durable governance or independent community evidence was observed.
rubric.2: Documented multi-party process or independent participation with limited standardization/adoption evidence.
rubric.3: Recognized standards governance or sustained independent multi-party adoption and maintenance.

cases.title: Author a multi-host scenario with an objective
cases.authored_requirement: Represent three networked hosts, service/software intent, two participant roles, and a success objective without implementation-specific credentials.
cases.unit_of_observation: One system-native authored artifact and its documented validation path.
cases.applicability_rule: Applicable when the system claims scenario, playbook, environment, or federation authoring for at least one named construct; otherwise record out of scope.
cases.permitted_assistance: Pinned official examples and reference documentation; no unstated extensions.
cases.inputs: A bounded prose brief naming topology, roles, service intent, and success condition.
cases.expected_artifact: A native artifact or source-grounded walkthrough identifying represented and unrepresented parts.

criteria.success: All applicable parts have native constructs and a documented validation path.
criteria.partial: At least one applicable part requires prose, code, or an external plane.
criteria.failure: The central authored unit cannot be represented within the system's declared scope.

cases.title: Compose and version reusable authored material
cases.authored_requirement: Reuse a separately identified authored unit, bind its revision, and state compatibility or replacement behavior.
cases.unit_of_observation: One composition/versioning walkthrough using the pinned source boundary.
cases.applicability_rule: Applicable to systems that accept reusable authored units; out of scope for pure runtime exchange with no authoring composition.
cases.permitted_assistance: Pinned standards, source, and official examples.
cases.inputs: A base unit, a dependent unit, and a requested revision change.
cases.expected_artifact: A native reference/import/sub-playbook/composition mechanism or an explicit unsupported result.

criteria.success: Identity, revision, composition, and compatibility behavior are explicit.
criteria.partial: Reuse exists but revision or compatibility behavior remains implicit.
criteria.failure: No native reuse/composition mechanism was found.

cases.title: Declare a controlled participant experiment
cases.authored_requirement: Declare participants, a task, factor levels, allocation or randomization, measures, evidence, and a study/run boundary.
cases.unit_of_observation: One source-grounded mapping from the brief to native constructs and named external obligations.
cases.applicability_rule: Applicable when experiment, evaluation, training, or agent-study claims are in scope; otherwise out of scope.
cases.permitted_assistance: Pinned standards, source, official examples, and ACES experiment contracts.
cases.inputs: A two-condition participant study with a preserved seed, outcome measure, and evidence requirement.
cases.expected_artifact: Native study/task/run constructs or a bounded declaration of external/missing concerns.

criteria.success: All design elements are first-class and version/provenance bound.
criteria.partial: Objectives or measures exist but allocation, study, evidence, or participant semantics are external or missing.
criteria.failure: No applicable experiment-design surface was observed.

cases.title: Reject a dangling authored reference
cases.authored_requirement: Introduce exactly one reference to an undeclared node, step, object, participant, or federation class.
cases.unit_of_observation: The documented or executable validation result for the single injected defect.
cases.applicability_rule: Applicable when the system has cross-object authored references; otherwise out of scope.
cases.permitted_assistance: Pinned parser tests, validation rules, standards text, or formal-analysis descriptions.
cases.inputs: A valid representative artifact plus one dangling identifier.
cases.expected_artifact: A bounded rejection/diagnostic or an explicit finding that the check is absent/not evidenced.

criteria.success: The production or normative validation boundary requires rejection with a useful location.
criteria.partial: The constraint is stated but executable rejection or diagnostics are not evidenced.
criteria.failure: The dangling reference is accepted or no validation rule was found.

cases.title: Reject contradictory authored constraints
cases.authored_requirement: Inject one contradiction between two otherwise valid constraints, branches, resource bounds, or required semantic outcomes.
cases.unit_of_observation: The formal, semantic, or normative result for the single contradiction.
cases.applicability_rule: Applicable when the system claims semantic, formal, workflow, or conformance validation; otherwise out of scope.
cases.permitted_assistance: Pinned formal semantics, validator tests, standards conformance rules, and source documentation.
cases.inputs: A valid representative artifact plus one mutually unsatisfiable condition.
cases.expected_artifact: Unsatisfiable/rejected result or a bounded not-evaluated finding.

criteria.success: The owning analysis detects the contradiction before successful execution/exchange.
criteria.partial: Only a bounded structural contradiction is detected or the rule lacks executable evidence.
criteria.failure: No applicable contradiction check was observed.

analysis_rules.primary_result: Publish the evidence surface and scope-qualified Pareto frontiers; do not publish a universal total score.
analysis_rules.pareto_scope: Compute dominance only within a declared scope stratum and only over axes applicable to every member of that group.
analysis_rules.missing_handling: Keep out-of-scope, not observed, not implemented, and not evaluated distinct; never coerce them to zero.
analysis_rules.weighting_policy: Predeclare bounded integer weight profiles before reading their rankings and retain every result.
analysis_rules.reversal_policy: If reasonable profiles change the first-ranked system, disclose the reversal and prohibit a weight-independent winner headline.
analysis_rules.quality_claim_policy: A highest-quality claim requires a separate validated quality construct and is not supported by this protocol.
analysis_rules.claim_evidence_policy: Every public claim records ADR-021 evidence status, threats to validity, a falsification protocol, objective pass/fail criteria, allowed and disallowed evidence, named evidence artifacts, and a derivation recomputed from the frozen observations.
